Bob Stewart was born in Sioux Fall, South Dakota on February 3, 1945 and spent his childhood in New York City and Newport, Rhode Island. He has played tuba in a wide variety of contexts and has taught at the high school and college levels. Bob’s recording as a leader include “First Line” (1987) and “Then and Now” (1996), where he explores the role of the tuba, past, present and future.
Bob was interviewed in Rome, New York on August 24, 2006 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe and we are filming for the Jazz Archive at Hamilton College and I’m very pleased to have Bob Stewart with me today. And I said to you a moment ago, you’re my first tuba interview. We have one banjo player and now we have a tuba player.
Yeah. So I’m pleased to be able to talk about your career. You’ve, probably like most musicians, worn a lot of hats in the music business.
